newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to build fast boats carrying missiles - paper.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to build fast boats carrying missiles - paper.

text.p: Taiwan's navy will build self-designed high-speed patrol boats carrying missiles to replace 50 existing missile-loaded vessels, the local China Times newspaper reported on Sunday.
The paper said the new boats would be large, but it did not specify capacity or weight. It did not mention how many the navy planned to build or how much it would cost.
The paper said the design of the new boats was almost complete, and the navy would soon seek to have tenders called to build them.
Navy officials were unvailable for comment, and a defence ministry spokesman said the ministry was unaware of the report.
"We could not comment now. ...So far we don't know anything about this," the spokesman said by telephone.
Taiwan has ordered six Lafayettte-class missile frigates from France and has taken delivery of two so far.
Taiwan maintains it needs advanced weapons to counter the rapid military modernisation of China, the island's arch rival since a civil war split them in 1949.

China held war games and missile tests in the Taiwan Strait in the weeks before Taiwan's presidential election in March 1996 in what Beijing acknowledged was a bid to dissuade the island from pursuing independence.
Beijing vows to retake Taiwan by force if the island opts for independence.
